summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput results from last week's perf runs, discuss continuous batching and queuing configuration, set concurrency targets, and align on next steps for a prod-like load test. We agreed to run a larger end-to-end benchmark with Novapay infra and iterate batching params; Redwood to send detailed configs and a dedicated capacity quote.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have 45 minutes — quick goal is to review last run's numbers and decide on next run parameters.
[00:18] Aisha Khan: Hi all, yep that's right, thanks Lena. We ran the baseline script yesterday, saw some spikes at peak.
[00:35] Miguel Santos: Cool, I'll pull the numbers up — so this is the run with 8 concurrent workers, batch size adaptive on the SE side. We got average throughput about 1.2k tokens/sec, p95 latency around 380ms, p99 around 780ms.
[01:02] Tom Reed: Right, and just to add, our target is roughly 50ms-100ms p95, and we need to support burst concurrency ~5k users. So current numbers are a ways off.
[01:25] Priya Menon: Also noticed the queue length climbed to 30 requests during the 2 minute spike, and retries started to happen.
[01:40] Lena Park: Okay, thanks. Two quick context points: the current run was on the hosted variant with auto-scale turned off, and quantized model (4-bit) to reduce memory. For throughput we usually tune continuous batching and concurrency targets — we want to balance latency SLOs vs token cost.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: Could you remind us what continuous batching settings you used? The config file we have shows batch_window_ms: 20, max_batch_size: 64.
[02:22] Miguel Santos: Yeah so batch_window_ms was 20ms, but we had concurrency cap at 8 so real batch sizes hovered 10-22 depending on arrival. The runtime does continuous batching, but with low concurrency you don't get big batches.
[02:41] Tom Reed: Makes sense. If we raise concurrency, do we risk p99 blowing up because of long queues?
[02:52] Miguel Santos: That's the tradeoff. Increasing concurrency increases batch formation, which improves tokens/sec and cost, but queueing can add latency. The trick is to tune both concurrency and batch_window so p95 is satisfied and p99 stays acceptable.
[03:12] Lena Park: Quick data point — in our internal tests with similar model family, moving from concurrency 8 to 40 with batch_window 25ms improved throughput 3.6x and p95 dropped to ~120ms while p99 was ~260ms. But that's on a dedicated pool with larger GPU memory and KV cache hits.
[03:36] Aisha Khan: We are using your hosted nodes in us-east-1 right now, right? Not dedicated.
[03:42] Lena Park: Correct, hosted. For production scale you might need dedicated capacity to reach the 5k concurrent target reliably.
[03:50] Priya Menon: If we go dedicated, how much of this is config vs needing more GPUs? We want to understand unit economics first.
[03:59] Miguel Santos: Both — better hardware gives headroom for larger batches and parallelism, but config matters: batch window, concurrency target, token cutoff, prefix cache residency. With a caching layer (prefix/KV cache) we can bypass recomputation for repeated context which helps p95 a lot.
[04:20] Tom Reed: Does Redwood's runtime support request queueing policies? We want FIFO vs priority for some latency-critical routes.
[04:29] Lena Park: Yes — the routing layer supports per-route queue policies and priority tiers. You can pin low-latency routes to a reserved slot and let less critical routesside queue longer. We can share defaults we recommend.
[04:42] Aisha Khan: Okay cool. Back to the numbers: Miguel, can you walk us through the CPU/GPU utilization during that run?
[04:51] Miguel Santos: Sure. GPU util peaked at ~68%, average 52%. CPU on the host was spiky up to 85% during batch assembly, which suggests we were CPU-bound at points; that suppresses effective concurrency.
[05:06] Priya Menon: Huh, so maybe we need to bump instance types or tune prefetch.
[05:11] Miguel Santos: Exactly. Also, we saw the KV cache hit rate was 12% on this workload; if you can increase locality or prefix reuse, a 40-60% hit rate is achievable and that dramatically cuts per-request compute.
[05:27] Tom Reed: How would we increase cache hit rate? Changes to prompt templates?
[05:31] Miguel Santos: Templates and request shaping — consistent system prompts, using short identifiers vs long context, truncation strategies. Redwood also supports a prefix caching API where you can prewarm caches for known flows.
[05:44] Aisha Khan: For the next run, we want to simulate prod like traffic — 5k concurrent users but with typical session lengths and request mix. Is Redwood able to coordinate a run with our infra?
[05:56] Lena Park: Yes, we can run the benchmark in collaboration — Miguel can provide a harness and we can ingest into your test cluster. We'll need SSH/access and test VPC details. Priya?
[06:07] Priya Menon: I can arrange access; will confirm by Friday.
[06:10] Miguel Santos: Great. For that run I propose these starting params: concurrency target 40, batch_window_ms 25, max_batch_size 128, token_cutoff 2k, and a per-route small-slot reserved capacity for 5% of traffic. That should increase batch sizes to ~60-80 in bursts.
[06:29] Tom Reed: Sounds good. What's the expected p95/p99 with that config on hosted?
[06:34] Miguel Santos: On hosted probably p95 ~150ms p99 ~350-420ms — but that's optimistic w/out dedicated GPUs and higher cache hits. With dedicated we see p95 ~90-120ms and p99 ~200-260ms in our internal runs.
[06:50] Aisha Khan: So dedicated looks likely if we want consistent SLOs. We'll need a cost estimate.
[06:55] Lena Park: I'll draft a dedicated capacity quote. For now let's run the prod-like test on hosted to baseline, then evaluate.
[07:03] Tom Reed: One more question — queue timeouts and backpressure. When queue hits threshold do you return an immediate 503 or a throttling token? We need graceful degradation.
[07:15] Miguel Santos: We support throttling headers and token-based backpressure; you can configure an adaptive fallback — if queue latency > X use a smaller model or return a partial token stream and capture for re-try. We can also do immediate 429 for non-critical routes.
[07:32] Priya Menon: Can you walk through our last spike? Why did retries happen?
[07:37] Miguel Santos: Looking at logs, a sudden burst increased arrival rate by 6x for ~90s; concurrency stayed at 8 so batches couldn't scale, queue length shot up and our retry policy kicked in. Also some of the requests had long prompt lengths which blocked batch turnover.
[07:56] Aisha Khan: Should we chunk long prompts?
[07:59] Miguel Santos: Yep, or enforce a token cap pre-arrival. Also consider async batch endpoints for long-running requests.
[08:08] Lena Park: Alright let's define the concrete next run: prod-like load, concurrency target 40, batch_window 25ms, max_batch 128, run length 30 minutes, workload mix randomized per your traffic matrix. Redwood provides harness and collects GPU/CPU/KV metrics. Agreed?
[08:27] Tom Reed: Agreed. Priya will confirm infra.
[08:30] Priya Menon: Yep.
[08:32] Aisha Khan: Can we also include a run with dedicated-like hardware? Maybe you can spin up a dedicated pool for a 2 hour test?
[08:40] Lena Park: We can do a limited dedicated burst test — I need to check internal ops calendar but yes we can propose a short dedicated window. I'll include that in the quote.
[08:49] Miguel Santos: For observability we'll add per-request token counts, batch size distribution, time-in-queue histogram and per-route latency percentiles. We'll push the raw logs and a summarized spreadsheet.
[09:03] Tom Reed: That'll be useful. On the config side, any quick wins we can try before the big run?
[09:09] Miguel Santos: Increase concurrency to 16 and batch_window to 30ms, that will give you a quick ~1.6x throughput uplift without major queueing. Also enable prefix prewarm for top 10 flows.
[09:22] Aisha Khan: Let's try those changes this week and then run the big test next week.
[09:27] Lena Park: Sounds good. Any security or compliance items to note for the dedicated test?
[09:32] Priya Menon: We'll need SOC2 scope confirmation, and KMS access patterns — we currently require a bring-your-own-key flow.
[09:39] Lena Park: Redwood supports BYOK and HSM integrations — I'll have our security brief attached.
[09:44] Tom Reed: Great. Aisha: anything else from product side?
[09:48] Aisha Khan: No, that's it. We'll watch for the spreadsheet.
[09:52] Lena Park: Okay recap: Miguel sends perf spreadsheet + logs and quick-win config by Friday; Priya confirms test cluster access; Lena sends dedicated capacity quote and security brief; schedule big run once infra confirmed.
[10:08] Tom Reed: Thanks all.
[10:10] Priya Menon: Thanks.
[10:12] Miguel Santos: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:15] Lena Park: Bye everyone.
